newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may limit trans-Siberian flights for Japan.
newsitem.headline: Russia may limit trans-Siberian flights for Japan.

text.p: Russia may restrict the rights of Japanese airlines to fly trans-Siberian routes after aviation authorities failed to reach agreement at talks in Japan, a Federal Aviation Service (FAS) official said on Sunday.

Sergei Seskutov, deputy head of the service's international department, told Reuters that Japan had rejected a Russian request for permission to fly to all destinations laid down in an agreement between the former Soviet Union and Japan.
"Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines can use only 41 percent of these rights while Japanese airlines use 98 percent," Seskutov said.
Aeroflot would like to fly to the northern Japanese city of Sapporo but Japan had refused permission, he said.
During the talks, which ended earlier this month, the Japanese side asked Russia for permission to use additional trans-Siberian air routes for its regular flights between Europe and Japan.
"We replied that first it would be necessary to achieve parity in the agreement," Seskutov said.
Russia may allow Japanese airlines to use only 41 percent of rights on trans-Siberian routes, he said. "It may be done."
Japanese airlines can operate only a limited number of flights over Siberia -- the most direct route to Europe -- and any further restrictions could greatly lengthen flights and prove costly.
Seskutov said Russia was interested in developing air links with Japan, but not in developing Japanese airlines' transit services between Europe and Japan.
Seskutov also said Russian carriers had had rights to operate flights between Tokyo, Bangkok and Seoul since 1973, but "they were only on paper".
Air services between Russia and Japan are still governed by the accord signed 23 years ago by Tokyo and the Soviet Union.
